author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, all on one page.
acceptance_criteria: Opening /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows, each under its stored name.
Each specialty lists the veterinarians holding it, named first name before last (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page; the page lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster.
All specialties appear together on one page, with nothing offering a further page.
A specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian shown under it.
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, appear in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one.
The page's own wording is supplied for every supported language, per REQ-LANG-002; stored specialty and veterinarian names are shown untranslated.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged, per the owner's recorded decision).
A navigation entry or an inbound link to the page from anywhere else; the owner recorded that a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request.
Changing the existing veterinarian directory, which stays paged and unchanged.
notes: Grounded in the intake-decision at line 1. Owner quote on scope: "A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2 is unchanged)." Owner quote on reachability: "The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come as a follow-up request." No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Three questions the request did not address are recorded in the PRD's Open Questions rather than raised: the visible entry point, whether an unheld specialty should appear (listed, on the narrowest reading that the page shows every specialty the clinic knows), and which order to present in (only stability required). REQ-LANG-002 binds every page, so new page wording needs all supported languages; the owner's "by its stored name" settles that specialty names are data, not wording.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the existing vet feature package and reuses every in-force pattern: Web controller, Repository, Thymeleaf template, message bundles. One adjustment is needed. VetRepository reaches specialties only through Vet, so a specialty no veterinarian holds is unreachable today; a second lookup repository supplies the full specialty set, mirroring PetTypeRepository in the owner package. Grouping and ordering go into a small immutable SpecialtyDirectory projection rather than into the controller, so architecture-principles.md's Web controller row (no business rule in a controller) is not breached again and the ordering criterion is unit-testable without MockMvc. No new module, dependency, pattern, or ADR.
integration_points: SpecialtyController is a new @Controller in the vet package serving GET /specialties.html; it depends on SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository by constructor injection and returns view name vets/specialtyList.

SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> with a single Collection<Specialty> findAll(), mirroring VetRepository's minimal-surface shape in the same package. Do not add @Cacheable: the vets cache has no eviction and the new read needs none.

SpecialtyDirectory is built by a static factory from the specialty collection and the veterinarian collection, and exposes the pairs to the template. Vet.getSpecialties() is eagerly fetched, so no extra query is needed for holders.
The template reuses fragments/layout with a menu argument matching no existing nav item, so no navigation markup changes and no page links here (the owner recorded the no-entry-point decision).
Existing message keys 'vets' and 'specialties' already carry the wording this page needs. Any genuinely new key must be added to messages.properties and to all nine non-English bundles.

patterns.description: lookup-value repository precedent: a repository for a non-aggregate lookup entity is established here, so SpecialtyRepository is consistency, not a new pattern
minimal Repository<T, Integer> marker interface with hand-declared read methods — the shape SpecialtyRepository copies
the owner package already holds one controller per HTTP surface (owner, pet, visit); a second controller in the vet package follows that precedent rather than growing VetController
page shape to copy: layout fragment replacement, th:text with #{} keys for all wording, th:each over a model attribute, stored names rendered untranslated
Value object row covers SpecialtyDirectory: immutable, equal by value, no identity, constructed valid; Web controller row forbids putting the grouping in the controller

risks.risk: Ordering by a database ORDER BY would vary with vendor collation; the PostgreSQL case-sensitivity defect on owner search is the recorded precedent.
risks.mitigation: Order inside SpecialtyDirectory with an explicit Java comparator — specialties by stored name, holders by last name then first name then id. Cover it with a SpecialtyDirectoryTests unit test; the prd-entry names no test for the stable-order criterion.

risks.risk: Veterinarians are read through VetRepository.findAll(), which is @Cacheable("vets") with no eviction configured (system-design.md Open Questions, item 5).
risks.mitigation: Accept: the application has no veterinarian write path, so the new page inherits exactly the staleness the existing vet list already has. Add no new cache.

risks.risk: The page renders every specialty and every holder with no paging, by product decision, so response size grows with the roster.
risks.mitigation: Accept at single-clinic scale; the seeded set is three specialties and six veterinarians. Record it rather than design paging the PRD excludes.

risks.risk: I18nPropertiesSyncTest scans every src/main HTML file for literal text and fails the build on a hard-coded string, and separately requires every base key in all nine non-English bundles.
risks.mitigation: Route all page wording through #{} keys; prefer the existing 'vets' and 'specialties' keys. A specialty no veterinarian holds renders an empty holder list rather than a new 'none' wording, which is the narrowest reading of the criterion and adds no key.

risks.risk: Stored specialty and veterinarian names are echoed into HTML.
risks.mitigation: Thymeleaf escapes expression output by default; use th:text and never th:utext. This is the same control the threat model records for the existing pages, and the slice introduces no new trust boundary — it is an unauthenticated read of data already public on /vets.html.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit. Durable-memory writes made by this dispatch: docs/system-design.md gains Contracts rows for SpecialtyController, SpecialtyRepository, and SpecialtyDirectory, adds REQ-SPECIALTYDIRECTORY-001 to the Specialty and VetRepository rows, notes that SpecialtyDirectory is assembled per request, and corrects the vet package line to plural repositories and controllers. No ADR: the slice reverses no decision and introduces no trade-off worth recording. Two deliberate deviations from the prd-entry's file_targets, which are guidance rather than contract: a new SpecialtyController instead of a second surface on VetController (owner-package precedent, and VetController's existing routes do not need the specialty repository), and a new SpecialtyRepository instead of a cross-entity @Query on VetRepository (that interface is typed to Vet). The five test_names in the prd-entry are unchanged and belong in SpecialtyControllerTests. Terms follow docs/ubiquitous-language.md: Specialty and Veterinarian in prose, Vet as the code short form. Open question left for a later slice, not raised as a consultation per the dispatch instruction: whether the specialty page should ever gain a visible entry point, which the owner recorded as a possible follow-up.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: No NVD verification ran in this review: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle and the reviewer has no network access. Treat the dependency posture as not verified rather than clean. The change set adds no artifact (build.gradle unchanged, Spring Boot pinned at 4.1.0 via the plugin), so the supply-chain delta for this slice is zero; closing the standing NVD check belongs to CI or a human.

Response size on /specialties.html grows with the whole specialty x vet_specialties join, unpaged by requirement, while the neighbouring /vets.html pages at 5. This is not attacker-controllable in this application — no route writes vets or specialties, so the row count is fixed by the seed data — which is why it is a note rather than a finding. Should a specialty or veterinarian write path ever land, this page becomes the amplification target and should be revisited.

SpecialtyController issues the specialty read and the veterinarian read as two separate transactions (the @Transactional(readOnly = true) sits on each repository method), so a concurrent write could produce a page assembled from two snapshots. Harmless for a read-only demonstration with no writer; worth knowing if the directory ever assembles under concurrent writes.
approved_aspects: XSS: every DB-derived value in src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders through th:text, so Thymeleaf's default escaping stays on. No th:utext anywhere in templates/ (swept with grep -F), and the new template introduces no __${...}__ preprocessing — the pre-existing preprocessing sites (layout.html, inputField.html, selectField.html, vetList.html) all take fragment-local literals or numeric page values, never request text. The concatenation inside th:text="${holder.firstName + ' ' + holder.lastName + ' '}" is an expression-level join whose result is still escaped on output.

Data access: SpecialtyRepository.findAll() is a Spring Data derived query with no string-built query text and no request-derived parameter. Injection-into-data-access row of docs/security-principles.md passes.

Least privilege at the repository: SpecialtyRepository extends the bare Repository marker and declares only findAll() with @Transactional(readOnly = true) — no write or delete method is exposed to reach a specialty row.

Mass assignment: SpecialtyController.showSpecialtyDirectory binds nothing from the request (Model only), so no identifier-binding surface exists and no @InitBinder disallow list is required. No @RequestParam, no @PathVariable, no command object.

Exposed-surface widening: the one new route GET /specialties.html is a read-only HTML page over specialty names and veterinarian full names — data already public through the existing /vets.html page and /vets representation. It mutates no state, touches no management endpoint, and leaves the baseline in docs/system-design.md § Security Context unchanged. PRD and system-design both state what it exposes, per the security-principles requirement that a new endpoint say so.
Path/resource resolution: the view name "vets/specialtyList" is a compile-time constant; no request-derived value composes a path or resource name.
Secrets and logging: the change adds no logging, no exception message, no credential, and no System.out/System.err. Nothing new can reach the error page, which renders exception messages.

Deserialization: no Jackson polymorphic typing, no @JsonTypeInfo, no XML parsing, no Java serialization introduced. SpecialtyDirectory and SpecialtyEntry are HTML-model-only types, not bound to any request or wire format.
Shell and process execution: none — grep for Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec( over the vet package is empty.

Concurrency: the singleton SpecialtyController holds only final repository references; SpecialtyDirectory's two static Comparators are stateless, and both record components are defensively copied with List.copyOf. Reading the shared @Cacheable("vets") collection is non-mutating — sorted() and the grouping map build new structures rather than reordering the cached list in place.
Supply chain: build.gradle is untouched by this change set — no new dependency, no repository change, no version move.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Eight files in one module, six of them new and none deleted: the change adds a route, a lookup repository, a projection, a template and two test classes, editing no existing production file. It reads the shared cached veterinarian collection but only streams and sorts it into fresh lists, so the cached state it borrows is never mutated. No sensitive paths.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading every hunk, the code does what the PRD entry describes. Holders are matched to specialties by Specialty id rather than instance identity, which is the right call given the specialty read and the veterinarian read come from separate repository calls; getOrDefault yields an empty holder list for an unheld specialty, matching edge case 1. Ordering is decided in Java by two named comparators rather than by database collation. The template concatenates each holder as first name, last name and a trailing space with no delimiter between holders, which is the same rendering convention vetList.html already uses for its specialty column.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert real outcomes and would fail against a broken implementation. Unit tests pin grouping, the unheld specialty, both ordering rules and the defensive copy; controller tests drive real Thymeleaf rendering through MockMvc with hand-written in-memory repository doubles and cover all four Done-when criteria plus the unheld-specialty edge case. The one untested comparator branch, the id tie-break, fires only between veterinarians sharing both names, whose rendered output is identical either way.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers the full-battery plan dispatched approved with zero findings, but two attached recommendations. The security reviewer states the dependency posture is not verified rather than clean, since no NVD check could run, and flags that the unpaged page grows with the whole specialty-to-veterinarian join and that the two repository reads sit in separate transactions. The test reviewer asks for a case covering the untested id tie-break.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions and zero consultations; the single build-retry record is a planned partial-artifact checkpoint that says so in its own text, not a gate failure. The changed paths match the design-block declared primary paths exactly, no navigation entry was added in line with the owner recorded decision, and the three new Open Questions record the choices the request left open rather than deciding them.

rationale: An additive, read-only page contained in the vet package, with tests covering every stated criterion. The residual is reviewer notes rather than defects: the supply-chain check never ran, so treat the dependency posture as unverified, and the page is unpaged over the full join. Read those before merging.
